title: Quantum Dynamics of Full Counting Statistics in Fermionic Lattices with Localized Gain
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of full counting statistics (FCS) of the growth of the total number of fermions in a one-dimensional non-interacting lattice subjected to a localized particle gain (source) at one edge. The dynamics of the setup is modeled by the Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) quantum master equation. We recast the counting problem that involves counting particle number at every lattice site to a problem where only the local injected site is involved. We employ the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral formalism within the GKSL framework and derive an analytical expression for the cumulant generating function at arbitrary times and obtain a Levitov-Lesovik type formula in the long-time limit, earlier derived for boundary driven setups in the steady-state. For clean lattices with either short- or long-range hopping, supporting single-particle delocalized eigenstates, we show that all cumulants grow linearly with time in the asymptotic regime. Our analytical results are in excellent agreement with direct numerical simulations. These findings establish a general framework for characterizing FCS and quantum fluctuations in driven open fermionic systems with localized particle injection.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the full counting statistics of fermionic particle number growth in driven quantum lattices. Using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, the authors derive the cumulant generating function, showing that the growth rate depends critically on the underlying lattice structure. The results distinguish between linear growth (for delocalized states) and non-linear growth (for localized states), providing a general diagnostic tool for open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dynamics of Full Counting Statistics (FCS) for the growth of the total number of fermions in a lattice driven by a localized particle source.
main_result: For clean lattices with delocalized states, all cumulants grow linearly with time in the long-time limit, while localized states can lead to non-linear growth, such as logarithmic time dependence.
method: The analysis employs the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral formalism within the GKSL quantum master equation framework to derive the cumulant generating function.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional non-interacting fermionic lattice subjected to a localized particle gain (source) modeled by the GKSL equation. The Hamiltonian can be generalized to include short- or long-range hopping interactions.
key_observables: Full Counting Statistics (FCS), characterized by the Cumulant Generating Function (CGF), $\chi(\lambda, t)$, and its cumulants ($\kappa_n$).
important_parameters: Localized injection strength ($\Gamma$), time ($t$), and the hopping range exponent ($\alpha$). The analysis distinguishes between the long-time limit (delocalized states) and the presence of localized states.
main_assumptions: The linear growth result assumes the underlying lattice possesses delocalized single-particle eigenstates and the thermodynamic limit ($L 	o \infty$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time dependence of the first three cumulants ($\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3$), confirming linear growth for delocalized systems and showing $\ln t$ growth for disordered/localized systems.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the GKSL framework, then applying the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral formalism to derive the CGF. It analyzes both the short-time and long-time limits, contrasting the linear growth found for clean lattices with the non-linear growth observed when disorder or localization is present.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general theoretical framework for characterizing quantum fluctuations and particle transport in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding energy/particle flow in quantum devices.
